title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Extended Version)
version: extended version published May 20, 2014 (Stanford tech report; USENIX ATC 2014 paper plus extra material)
why: Primary definition of the log machinery: AppendEntries RPC and consistency check, the Log Matching Property, nextIndex backtracking, the commit rule with the Figure 8 scenario.

title: Consensus: Bridging Theory and Practice (PhD dissertation)
why: Longer authoritative treatment of Raft log replication, commitment and the safety proof, with errata and formal-spec appendix the paper lacks.

title: Students' Guide to Raft
why: Checklist of the AppendEntries, nextIndex/matchIndex and commitIndex mistakes MIT 6.824 implementers actually made, including why log[N].term == currentTerm is required.

title: 6.5840 Lecture 6: RSM and Raft (1)
why: Frames the replicated log's purpose and gives a concrete multi-term log-divergence example that motivates the repair and commit rules.

title: 6.5840 Lecture 7: Raft (2)
why: Walks a full log-repair trace and derives the fast conflict-backup scheme (XTerm/XIndex/XLen) plus the two meanings of committed behind Figure 8.

title: etcd raft package: raft.go and log.go
why: Production Go implementation showing handleAppendEntries, maybeAppend/findConflict truncation and the currentTerm check in maybeCommit.

title: raft.tla: TLA+ specification of Raft
version: raft.tla at commit 6ecbdbcf1bcde2910367cdfd67f31b0bae447ddd (2025-02-18); differs slightly from dissertation Appendix B
why: Machine-readable formal spec to check exact AppendEntries, log-append and commit conditions against a real implementation.

title: Raft Refloated: Do We Have Consensus?
version: ACM SIGOPS Operating Systems Review 49(1), January 2015
why: Independent reimplementation that restates the commitment subtlety with its own worked Leader-Completeness violation and reports a livelock caused by that rule.
